expected.title: Reading Travel Conditions
expected.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Reading Travel Conditions.

Seafaring needs knowledge of water, weather, routes and the boat. People learned through experience and teaching.

Winds and currents can affect a journey. A planned route may need to change when conditions change.

Careful preparation reduces risks but cannot promise a safe trip in every situation.

Investigate the three clues below. Use them to decide what a careful learner should do in the teaching situation. You may revisit any clue before choosing.

routeActivity.title: Choose a Route for Today
routeActivity.instructions: Compare the travel clues with all three route descriptions. Choose a plan, check it, then explain why the conditions matter.
routeActivity.mapDescription: A symbolic route board, not a geographic map. All choices travel from the same island landing toward a neighboring community. The descriptions give all the information needed; no dragging or map reading is required.
conditions: The destination is a neighboring community across the water.
Your small boat is in good condition, but it is not suited to rough open water.
Today, the exposed crossing has rough waves. A sheltered coastal route has calmer conditions and a known landing.
The shallow creek shortcut has rocks and too little water for this boat. The crew can wait and check conditions again if they change.

routes.name: Open-water crossing
routes.description: A short exposed crossing with rough waves today. The boat is not suited to these conditions.
routes.feedback: A shorter route is not always a suitable route. Today the rough exposed water does not suit this boat. Compare the other conditions.

routes.name: Sheltered coastal route
routes.description: A longer route with calmer water today and a landing the crew knows. The crew will continue checking conditions.
routes.feedback: This plan fits the boat, today's calmer conditions and the known landing. It is suitable for this made-up situation, not a promise that any real route is always safe. Now explain why checking conditions matters.

routes.name: Shallow creek shortcut
routes.description: A short narrow creek with rocks and too little water for this boat.
routes.feedback: Calm-looking water can still be unsuitable. Rocks and low water make this shortcut a poor choice for this boat. Check the depth and boat clues.

fields.decisionSituation: You chose a route using the boat, water and landing clues. Now explain your plan. This is a fictional classroom example, not advice for a real sea journey.
fields.decisionQuestion: Why should the crew keep checking conditions even after choosing a route?
decisionChoices: Water and weather can change, so the crew may need to wait or revise the plan.
A longer route guarantees safety in every situation.
A familiar landing means weather never matters.
The shortest route must always be chosen.
fields.decisionCorrectAnswer: Water and weather can change, so the crew may need to wait or revise the plan.
fields.decisionExplanation: The route fits the stated conditions today. Conditions can change, and a crew may need a different plan. The exercise teaches comparing evidence, not guaranteeing real-world safety.
